header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Another important tool is mechanistic analysis, i.e. studying the model's weights and activations for understanding how it functions, which has been shown to fully explain the behavior of entire neural networks (Nanda et al., 2023; Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.quote: But the truth is that we’ve only scratched the surface of understanding a single vision model.

args.text:
Verdict: not supported

Olah et al. (2020), *Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits*, describes understanding individual neurons and circuits, with examples involving circles, dog heads, cars, and simple logic—not a complete explanation of an entire network’s behavior. distill:zoom-in/r1/b7 distill:zoom-in/r1/b8

The authors explicitly state: "But the truth is that we’ve only scratched the surface of understanding a single vision model." distill:zoom-in/r1/b11 They also qualify their central claims: "These claims are deliberately speculative." distill:zoom-in/r1/b18

Thus, this cited source supports progress in understanding particular mechanisms, but does not support the claim that entire neural networks have been fully explained. distill:zoom-in/r1/b8 distill:zoom-in/r1/b11

There is also a discrepancy in the supplied sentence: the library’s version of *Model evaluation for extreme risks* defines mechanistic analysis and cites Nanda and Olah, but does not contain the added assertion about fully explaining entire networks. arxiv:2305.15324/v2/p12
